newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS -cash up 3/4,workweek data off.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS -cash up 3/4,workweek data off.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained around three-quarters of a point in fairly active trade at midday on Friday as the market drove higher on a surprising drop in the average weekly hours seen in payrolls data.

The latest payrolls data were scrutinized intently after the Federal Reserve's policy making arm signaled in mid-December comments released on Thursday that it was paying particular heed to any signs that a tighter labor market would produce inflationary pressures.

Even though the federal Labor Department said payrolls rose 271,000 in January, a bit higher than forecast, traders focused on the drop in average weekly hours to 34.1 from 34.8. And average earnings per hour only rose one cent to $12.06. The unemployment rate firmed one percentage point to 5.4 percent.
"We're up at least an 0.05 (in the long-end)," a trader said. "Actually, it's workweek euphoria," another said, explaining that was the key factor responsible for the bond market's rise.

Traders said that while activity in the secondary market picked up, with a number of sizable bid-wanted lists being circulated, selling pressure did appear big enough to dampen prices. "It seems fairly average...it's not like there's a huge flood of selling," one said.

The market was looking ahead to a rise in supplies of new issues that is expected next week, as the calender shows a total of around $2.7 billion of competitive and negotiated issues. That is about $1.1 billion more than the slim supplies seen this week.
A total of 48 competitive deals are scheduled for next week, totaling $886 million. Thirty-eight negotiated deals are expected totaling $1.82 billion.

The top competitive deal is expected to be Thursday's $250 million Illinois sale. The top negotiated deal is expected to be a $264 million Harris County Health Facilities Development Authority, Texas, offering via Smith Barney Inc.
And the negotiated calender includes an $82 million sale of general obligation bonds by Hempstead, New York, on Friday.
March municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade gained 22 ticks to 116-9/32, while March Treasury futures rose 25 ticks to 112-22/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 115 ticks.
In the secondary market, Dade County Florida Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.63 percent, NET, down four basis points.
Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority Illinois Dedicated State Tax Revenues of June 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.72 percent, NET, down eight basis points.
